text:
alan: Heads up — I'm putting a proposal on the table for a mixed control-plane attachment pattern that lets a tenant use both peered control-plane connections and private endpoints. Low overhead for onboarding, but we need clear failover semantics and interface boundaries. Thoughts?

mira: Can you sketch the failure modes you're worried about? is this for Dedicated customers primarily?

alan: Primary target is Dedicated + Private customers who want lower latency but still want a backstop path during endpoint maintenance. Failure modes: peering route flaps, private endpoint cert expiry, control-plane auth token drift. Need deterministic routing precedence.

devon: We should be explicit about the ordering: prefer private endpoint if healthy, fall back to peering if endpoint unavailable. But what counts as "unavailable"? TCP health only? Auth failure?

alan: Good point. Proposal: availability = (tcp + TLS handshake + cert validity + handshake auth). If any of those fail for >30s, switch to peering. Add hysteresis window (60s) to avoid flip-flopping.

sre-bot: automated note: existing probe interval is 10s, probe timeout 3s. If we change semantics we must update runbooks.

jess: Love the hysteresis. Also: who owns fallback routing logic? control plane or tenant-side agent? Prefer central control plane to avoid N* complexity in agents.

kevin: Centralizing simplifies rollout but creates trust boundary issues for Private deployments (customers that don't want us announcing routes into their VPC). Could be a toggle: customer-managed agent decision vs RP-managed central routing.

mira: That matches our product tiers. For Private/on-prem: agent makes the decision locally. For Redwood-managed Dedicated: control plane can decide and push route policy to regional relays. Document this in the API as `attachment_preference` enum 

alan: Example enum: `attachment_preference: ["private_first", "peering_first", "peering_only", "private_only"]`. Default for Dedicated = private_first, for Private = private_only.

jess: How do we surface observability? Need per-tenant metrics: current_attachment, last_switch_ts, switch_reasons (tls|tcp|auth|manual). Also alerts if >3 switches in 10m.

devon: Agree. Also suggest tagging requests in traces with attachment_id so we can trace a latency/cost delta between paths.

kevin: Security note: when switching to peering, we must ensure the auth tokens presented are scoped the same and no elevation happens. If agent handles decision, token refresh must be atomic with switch to avoid 401 storms.

alan: Implementation sketch for agent-local decision (pseudo):

```
probe_loop:
  every 10s: check tcp->tls->auth
  if failed for >30s: set prefer_peering=true; record last_switch_ts
  if healthy for >60s: set prefer_peering=false
  push status to cp via status-agg API
```

mira: For control-plane driven switch, we'll need a small API: `/v1/attachments/{id}/force_pref` with audit trail and a reconcile loop to ensure relays obey. Add RBAC so only ops roles or customer admin can trigger.

devon: Rollout strategy: start with internal tenants + 2 pilot customers, run for 2 weeks, verify switch counts and no auth regressions. Then opt-in for more customers, finally flip default for new Dedicated tenants.

jess: One more: migration path when both exist and we want to decommission peering. Need a graceful drain: mark prefer_private, set `deprecate_peering_ts`, and allow a month before route withdrawal. Add a preflight check that no active connections remain.

kevin: Ops playbook additions: how to force route back to peering, how to revoke peering quickly during a security event, and how to coordinate cert rotation to avoid simultaneous failovers.

alan: Thanks — I'll put this in an RFC-followup doc with the enum, API shapes, health probe thresholds, and a rollout checklist per the suggestions. @mira @devon @jess please review the draft when posted. :thumbsup:
